title: MALADE: Orchestration of LLM-powered Agents with Retrieval Augmented Generation for Pharmacovigilance

live_model.evidence: In the evaluations of MALADE, we consider two LLMs, GPT-4 Turbo and GPT-4o (Section 5.2); Table 1 'GPT-4 Turbo AUC with confidence 0.831 0.851'

prompt.location: Appendix B.1 (full prompts to DrugFinder, DrugAgent Critic, FDAHandler, CategoryAgent and its Critic)
prompt.note: All agent system prompts are printed; the orchestration logic is described in Section 4 and Appendix B.

claim.location: Table 1, row 'GPT-4 Turbo AUC with confidence', column ADE-based

data.source: OMOP ADE ground-truth table (10 drug categories x 10 outcomes, 55 evaluable pairs) and FDA drug labels via the OpenFDA API

notes: arXiv Aug 2024 with no preview string, so resolved to the GA snapshot; code at github.com/jihyechoi77/malade. Re-execution without code requires rebuilding the Langroid multi-agent loop, RAG over FDA labels and OpenFDA tool calls, hence 'maybe'. Authors note nondeterminism; no temperature stated.

resolution.plan: All agent prompts are printed (Appendix B.1) but the number depends on the Langroid orchestration (DrugFinder, DrugAgent and Critic, FDAHandler with vector-DB RAG over FDA labels and the OpenFDA tool, CategoryAgent and Critic), the label post-processing (Appendix B.4) and the confidence-to-score mapping behind the AUC, which are only in the repository. Take the pipeline from the repo, run it with gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 on the 55 evaluable OMOP category/outcome pairs, and compute the ADE-based AUC from the confidence scores (0.851).
resolution.approximation: FDA label content and OpenFDA responses drift over time; the authors report nondeterminism and no temperature.
